spec.description: Right-pointing convex kite with a circle tangent to all four sides; no centre, radii or subdivision lines appear in the question.
spec.mathematics: Left adjacent sides are a; right adjacent sides are b. Circle geometry is derived from equal distances to the four side lines. Coordinates are drawing parameters, not numerical givens.

answer.short:
$r=\dfrac{A}{a+b}$.

The four triangles have common perpendicular height $r$, so $A=r(a+b)$.
answer.worked:
Join the circle's centre to the four vertices. Each triangle has perpendicular height $r$, since the radius to a tangent is perpendicular to that side.
$$\begin{align*}A&=2\left(\frac{ar}{2}\right)+2\left(\frac{br}{2}\right)\\A&=ar+br\\A&=r(a+b).\end{align*}$$
Therefore $r=\dfrac{A}{a+b}$.
